statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress eases to 54 in the elevated band: the Saudi East-West pipeline is still shut with no restart timeline, WTI is marked $100.05 and a Wednesday policy decision is priced near 87 percent for an increase, while this hour's new verified developments are de-escalatory. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and Friday's advance was broad, with seven of eight tracked megacaps higher and semiconductor gains led by ARM, QCOM and INTC rather than a single narrow leader. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, eleven hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. Third, every new verified development in this hour leans de-escalatory: Riyadh welcomed Baghdad's pledge not to retaliate, Iraq dismissed two senior officials over the Maysan-origin drones, Tehran denied involvement through official channels, and the BRICS group called for maximum restraint. No evidence-based danger window is published, because no window inside this horizon contains a tradeable session. Stress at 54 describes an unresolved Gulf supply picture and a hawkishly priced policy week; under the fixed mapping Stress does not alter the machine state on its own.
headline: Fifteen hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, and Saturday's verified developments continue to lean de-escalatory: Riyadh has welcomed Baghdad's pledge not to retaliate, Iraq has dismissed two senior officials over the drones that shut the East-West pipeline, Tehran has denied involvement, and BRICS has urged maximum restraint.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found the price picture unchanged. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95% with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%, a curve consistent with a hawkish policy path rather than a growth scare. Friday's participation was broad rather than narrow: seven of the eight tracked megacaps closed higher, and semiconductor strength came from ARM at +4.17%, QCOM at +2.88% and INTC at +2.61% while NVDA finished essentially flat. Broad participation of that kind is a poor precursor to the squeeze-type one-way structure this Tail score is built to detect.

The macro backdrop is hawkish and already priced. Friday's inflation print showed headline consumer prices up 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year with core slightly above consensus, and CME FedWatch placed the odds of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September meeting at 86.7%, up from 72.4% the prior day. Equities rose anyway, which reporting attributed to the retreat in crude rather than to the inflation data itself. That meeting carries updated economic projections and a press conference thirty minutes after the decision, and the inherited calibration treats a multi-stage policy sequence as a case for care rather than an automatic block. Those are Wednesday checkpoints and sit outside this twenty-four-hour horizon.

The Gulf supply picture is the live unresolved item, and it moved in a de-escalatory direction again this hour. Saudi Arabia's 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline, which had been moving four to five million barrels a day or roughly four to five percent of global supply around the Strait of Hormuz, remains shut as a precaution while specialist teams assess damage south of Medina; no restart timeline has been published, though a comparable pumping-station repair in April took three days. Against that, Riyadh has welcomed Baghdad's pledge not to retaliate, Iraq has dismissed two senior officials after confirming the drones originated from its territory, Iran has denied involvement through official channels, and the BRICS group has called for maximum restraint. Crude settled lower on Friday in response to Gulf-Iranian contacts on Hormuz, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81%, and WTI at $100.05, down 2.37%.

The binding constraint on this assessment is structural rather than informational. CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC Sunday, eleven hours after the last slot in this horizon. Every forecast hour therefore describes a market with no tape, in which shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension and holding near session extremes cannot be observed because they cannot occur. Conditional Tail rises from 6 to a ceiling of 11 across the horizon, and that drift is an accruing reopen-gap premium for unpriced weekend headlines, not a directional view. Shared supplementary cross-asset context was older than its ninety-minute freshness bound this hour and was therefore treated as stale; it was in any case fully redundant with the independently verified primary data above, so it did not affect any score.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 12:00 UTC on 11 September to 11:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens on the 12:30 UTC inflation print, which produced the only elevated readings of the period: Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and then 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced from its 29,040.50 low, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then fell to 13 and 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final fourteen slots sit at Tail 5 and 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 88 to 55 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, eleven hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then drifts to 7, 8, 9, 10 and a ceiling of 11 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs 54 to a 58 ceiling and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage with no restart date, WTI marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach, and a 16 September policy decision with projections priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to 80, remaining inside the high band because the evidence set is complete and primary-sourced; the limitation is the freshness of price, not the coverage. The named checkpoints outside this horizon are the Sunday evening futures reopen, the Monday foreign ministers' meeting in Salalah and Wednesday's policy decision.
